## Summary

`tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py::test_push_loop_converges_under_contention`
(added one commit ago by 4c4f, `f7aa0d5b5`) failed in CI on a change that provably
cannot affect it, then the same test passed 18/18 locally on that same patch set.

Observed once so far: GitHub Actions run **30665788197** (Gerrit change 1134, patch set 1,
`gerrit-verify`), worker `popen-gw1`, ubuntu-latest, py3.13, git 2.54.0.

## Evidence

Failure output:

```
rc=1
competitor pushes fired=1
stdout:
Local tickets branch is ahead by 1 commit(s) — pushing.
stderr:
Push failed (non-retryable, exit 1): To .../origin.git
 ! [rejected]        HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)
```

That message is emitted at `reconcile-bridge.yml:321`, the ELSE arm of the classifier at
`:314`:

```sh
if echo "$push_stderr" | grep -qiE 'non-fast-forward|rejected|fetch first'; then
```

The stderr shown contains BOTH `rejected` and `fetch first`, so the classifier should have
matched and taken the retry arm. It did not. On attempt 1 the competitor had already
pushed (`competitor pushes fired=1`), so this is the ordinary benign-contention path the
test exists to cover.

## What has been ruled out

- **Not caused by change 1134.** Its only in-loop edit is `:319`, inside the THEN arm —
  unreachable in a run that took the ELSE arm. Its other edit (the pre-loop fetch)
  demonstrably worked, since `:299` printed an ahead-count that requires `origin/tickets`
  to have resolved.
- **Not the classifier's pattern.** 20,000 iterations of the exact `grep -qiE` against the
  exact stderr text from the failing run, under `set -euo pipefail`, produced 0
  misclassifications — so a `pipefail`/SIGPIPE interaction on that pipeline is not
  reproducible at this payload size.
- **Not reproducible locally.** 18/18 passes on the failing patch set (10 serial, 8 under
  parallel load), macOS, git 2.55.0.

## Leads not yet tested

- Whether `push_stderr` was actually EMPTY at classification time and the text in the
  `:321` message came from a later expansion — i.e. `push_stderr=$(git push ... 2>&1)`
  losing its capture under load. This is the leading hypothesis and is untested.
- git 2.54.0 (CI) vs 2.55.0 (local) behavioural difference in what `git push` writes to
  stderr vs stdout under `2>&1` capture.
- CPU starvation on a loaded runner perturbing the competitor shim's 6-subprocess sequence.

## Why this matters

The test gates every change through `gerrit-verify`, so a flake here costs a full CI cycle
per occurrence and trains reviewers to `recheck` reflexively. It also guards a real
convergence property (bug 4c4f), so weakening or skipping it is not the answer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The mechanism is reproduced deterministically (e.g. under enforced CPU contention or
      git 2.54.0) rather than inferred.
- [ ] Root cause named at a specific changeable artifact — the workflow's stderr capture,
      the classifier, or the test harness's shim.
- [ ] Fixed without weakening the convergence assertions the test exists to make.
- [ ] File paths: `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml`,
      `tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py`.
